newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Cullen yet to receive concrete offers.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Cullen yet to receive concrete offers.

text.p: Christian Cullen's manager Craig Loach said on Wednesday he had yet to receive any firm offers from provincial rugby unions chasing the services of the star All Black fullback.

Otago has reportedly offered $200,000 for the Manawatu youngster -- prompting Wellington to drop their interest because of the expense -- but Loach said Otago had not made a written offer and there had been no mention of astronomical figures.
The only discussion of money had been briefly with Manawatu, he said.
"A couple of first-division unions have shown interest in him but they have been verbal inquiries," said Loach.
"Over the last couple of days we've had a look at what they have had to say but we haven't made any decisions."
Loach said the unions were pushing the quality of their provinces ahead of money because the transfer fees in place meant a huge outlay for Cullen.
The manager said the two unions had been told to express their interest in writing and then he and Cullen would arrange meetings.
"Christian is relaxed about the whole thing. There's nothing definite. He is looking at what his options are.
"He's pretty happy in Palmerston North, he has a house here and his family lives just down the road (in Paekakariki)," Loach said.
There was also question of which Super 12 side to play for and outside the Auckland Blues, there was little between the other four sides.
